An accumulator adds a varying amount. The exam distinguishes them by WHAT is added, not by the variable name.","topic":"Loop vocabulary","id":"wr_p4_7","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What is a sentinel value?","options":["A special value that marks the end of a list of input data","A value that cannot be converted to another type","The first value read before a loop begins","The largest value a variable can hold"],"correct":0,"explain":"A sentinel (a \"dummy\" value such as 0 or -1) is not real data — it signals STOP. It must be a value that could never occur naturally in the data, or genuine records would end the loop early.","topic":"Loop vocabulary","id":"wr_p4_8","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What is a priming read?","options":["An input statement placed before the loop so the first value is available to the first test","Reading a file twice to check for errors","The first calculation performed inside a loop","Reading the sentinel value at the end of the data"],"correct":0,"explain":"The priming read fetches the first value BEFORE the loop condition is tested; a matching read at the bottom of the body fetches each following value. Without it, the first test has nothing to examine.","topic":"Loop vocabulary","id":"wr_p4_9","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What causes an infinite loop?","options":["The counter is initialised to 0 instead of 1","The loop body contains a nested if","The loop runs more than 1,000 times","Nothing in the body ever changes the value tested by the loop condition"],"correct":3,"explain":"A loop ends only when its condition becomes false. If the body never alters the variable in that condition — or alters it in the wrong direction — the test stays true forever. Running many times is not the same as running forever.","topic":"Loop vocabulary","id":"wr_p4_10","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What are the three basic structures from which all programs can be built?","options":["Input, processing, and output","Sequence, selection, and loop (iteration)","Analysis, design, and implementation","Variables, constants, and operators"],"correct":1,"explain":"The structure theorem says sequence, selection and loop are enough to express any program. Input-process-output describes the flow of DATA, and analysis-design-implementation names the development PHASES — different lists that are offered as distractors.","topic":"Program structures","id":"wr_p4_11","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What is the null case in a selection?","options":["A condition that cannot be evaluated","The branch where no action is taken","A loop that never executes","A variable that has not been given a value"],"correct":1,"explain":"In a single-alternative if, the false path does nothing — that empty path is the null case. It is a legitimate branch, not an error.","topic":"Selection structures","id":"wr_p4_12","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which loop is guaranteed to execute its body at least once?","options":["for each","while","for","do . . . while"],"correct":3,"explain":"A do-while tests its condition AFTER running the body, so the body always runs at least once. while and for test first, so they can run zero times if the condition starts false.","topic":"Loop vocabulary","id":"wr_p4_13","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which structure repeats a block a known, fixed number of times?","options":["A for loop with a counter","A while loop with a sentinel","A do-while loop","A dual-alternative if"],"correct":0,"explain":"When the number of repetitions is known in advance, a counter-controlled for loop is the natural fit. A sentinel-controlled while is used when you do NOT know how many values are coming.","topic":"Loop vocabulary","id":"wr_p4_14","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What is a module (also called a subroutine, procedure, method, or function)?","options":["A named block of statements that can be called from elsewhere in the program","A structure that repeats until a condition is false","A variable that can hold more than one value","A comment that explains a block of code"],"correct":0,"explain":"Modules let you write a task once and call it by name wherever it is needed, which supports reuse and top-down design. The many names come from different languages naming the same idea.","topic":"Modularity","id":"wr_p4_15","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What does a RETURN statement do inside a module?","options":["It restarts the module from the beginning","It ends the entire program immediately","It prints a value to the screen","It sends a value back to the statement that called the module"],"correct":3,"explain":"RETURN hands a value back to the caller, which can then store or use it. Printing is a separate action — a module can return a value without displaying anything.","topic":"Modularity","id":"wr_p4_16","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What is the scope of a variable?","options":["The part of the program in which that variable can be accessed","The number of times the variable is used","The range of values the variable can hold","The amount of memory the variable occupies"],"correct":0,"explain":"Scope is about WHERE a name is visible. A variable declared inside a module is local: it exists only during that call and cannot be seen outside it. The range of values is the data type, not the scope.","topic":"Modularity","id":"wr_p4_17","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What is the difference between a parameter and an argument?","options":["They are the same thing under different names","A parameter is returned and an argument is received","A parameter is always a number and an argument is always text","A parameter is the variable in the module header; an argument is the actual value passed in the call"],"correct":3,"explain":"The header declares parameters (placeholders). The call supplies arguments (real values) that fill them. Reversing the two is the classic exam trap.","topic":"Modularity","id":"wr_p4_18","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"In a flowchart, which symbol represents a decision?","options":["A parallelogram","A diamond","A rectangle","An oval"],"correct":1,"explain":"Diamond = decision (a yes/no branch). Parallelogram = input/output. Rectangle = processing. Oval = terminal (start/stop). These four cover almost every flowchart question.","topic":"Flowcharts","id":"wr_p4_19","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"In a flowchart, which symbol represents input or output?","options":["A parallelogram","An oval","A rectangle","A diamond"],"correct":0,"explain":"A parallelogram is input/output — reading a value or displaying one. A rectangle is a processing step such as a calculation.","topic":"Flowcharts","id":"wr_p4_20","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What does an end-structure statement (such as END IF or END WHILE) do?","options":["It resets the loop control variable","It marks where a structure finishes, so the reader knows which statements belong to it","It stops the program from running","It converts pseudocode into a programming language"],"correct":1,"explain":"End-structure statements delimit a block. Without them — or without indentation — it is ambiguous which statements sit inside the if or the loop.","topic":"Program structures","id":"wr_p4_21","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What is an abstract (high-level) step in a design?","options":["A comment ignored by the computer","A step written in a real programming language","A step that states WHAT must happen without yet saying HOW","A step that cannot be implemented"],"correct":2,"explain":"Top-down design starts with abstract steps and refines each into concrete ones. \"Calculate the payroll\" is abstract; the arithmetic that does it is the concrete refinement.","topic":"Modularity","id":"wr_p4_22","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which is the best reason to use a named constant instead of a literal value?","options":["Constants prevent all logic errors","Constants use less memory than variables","One meaningful name documents the value and it can be changed in a single place","Constants make the program run faster"],"correct":2,"explain":"A named constant such as TAX_RATE explains what the number means and is changed in one place instead of hunting for every 0.07. That is a readability and maintenance benefit, not a speed one.","topic":"Variables","id":"wr_p4_23","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What is a scalar variable, as opposed to a composite one?","options":["It holds a group of related values","It cannot be changed once set","It holds a single value at a time","It exists only inside a module"],"correct":2,"explain":"A scalar holds one value. A composite (an array or list, a record) groups several under one name. A value that cannot change is a constant — a different idea.","topic":"Variables","id":"wr_p4_24","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Why is indentation used in pseudocode?","options":["It marks where comments begin","It is required for the program to compile","It shows which statements belong inside a structure","It makes the program run faster"],"correct":2,"explain":"Pseudocode is read by people, and indentation makes the block structure visible at a glance. It carries no meaning for a compiler — pseudocode is never compiled.","topic":"Program structures","id":"wr_p4_25","difficulty":"medium"}],"D684/write_drill/p5":[{"text":"A software development team is building a desktop application for recording and mastering music tracks. Because of the complicated nature of this application, they decide to follow the software development lifecycle (SDLC) process. Which step will the team expect to start with?","options":["Test the program","Plan the logic","Code the program","Understand the problem"],"correct":3,"explain":"The cycle always begins by UNDERSTANDING THE PROBLEM — gathering requirements and constraints, and finding out what the users actually need. Planning the logic (flowcharts and pseudocode) comes second, and coding only after that. You cannot design a solution to a problem you have not pinned down.","topic":"Development cycle order","id":"wr_p5_1","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which step of the program development cycle is where flowcharts and pseudocode are produced?","options":["Translate the code","Plan the logic","Code the program","Understand the problem"],"correct":1,"explain":"\"Plan the logic\" is the design step: you work out the sequence of steps using tools such as flowcharts and pseudocode, before writing any language-specific code.","topic":"Development cycle order","id":"wr_p5_2","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What happens during the \"translate the code\" step?","options":["The program is installed for end users","The programmer rewrites the program in a second language","The requirements are converted into a flowchart","A compiler or interpreter converts the source code into a form the machine can run"],"correct":3,"explain":"Translation is the compiler or interpreter turning human-readable source into machine-runnable form. Syntax errors surface here — the translator cannot accept a statement that breaks the language rules.","topic":"Development cycle","id":"wr_p5_3","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A team has just finished coding and translating a program with no remaining syntax errors. What is the next step?","options":["Test the program","Understand the problem","Maintain the program","Plan the logic"],"correct":0,"explain":"A clean translation only proves the grammar is right. Testing with many sample inputs is what shows whether the program does the right THING — it is where logic errors are caught.","topic":"Development cycle order","id":"wr_p5_4","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A video game company follows the SDLC and has just put its finished game on sale to customers. Which step comes next?","options":["Maintain the program","Translate the code","Plan the logic","Test the program"],"correct":0,"explain":"Once a program is in production, the remaining work is MAINTENANCE — fixing defects users find, and making updates as needs change. Software lives far longer in maintenance than it spent being written.","topic":"Development cycle order","id":"wr_p5_5","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which phase of the software lifecycle typically consumes the most time and cost over a product's life?","options":["Implementation","Design","Testing","Maintenance"],"correct":3,"explain":"Programs are maintained for years after release, so maintenance normally outweighs the original development effort. That is also why readable code and good documentation pay off.","topic":"Development cycle","id":"wr_p5_6","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A program compiles and runs but always prints the wrong total. What kind of error is this?","options":["A logic error","A translation error","A syntax error","A hardware error"],"correct":0,"explain":"If it runs, the grammar was acceptable, so it is not a syntax error. Producing the wrong result means the instructions themselves are wrong — a logic error, which only testing will reveal.","topic":"Errors","id":"wr_p5_7","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A programmer types \"prnt total\" instead of \"print total\". What kind of error is this?","options":["A logic error","A syntax error","A runtime data error","A design error"],"correct":1,"explain":"A misspelled keyword breaks the language rules, so the translator rejects it — a syntax error. Logic errors are grammatically valid but do the wrong thing.","topic":"Errors","id":"wr_p5_8","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"In the analysis phase, what is the programmer mainly producing?","options":["A maintenance schedule","Working source code","A compiled executable","A clear statement of the requirements and constraints"],"correct":3,"explain":"Analysis is about understanding: what the program must do, what data it needs, and what limits apply. The output is understanding and documentation, not code.","topic":"SDLC phases","id":"wr_p5_9","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which activity belongs to the design phase?","options":["Fixing a defect reported by a user","Choosing the algorithms and data structures the program will use","Writing the source code","Running the program with test data"],"correct":1,"explain":"Design turns the understood problem into a plan — algorithms, structures, and the layout of the solution. Coding, testing and fixing all come later.","topic":"SDLC phases","id":"wr_p5_10","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What is the purpose of the testing phase?","options":["To gather requirements from the users","To translate the source code into machine language","To run the program with many inputs, including extremes, to confirm it behaves correctly","To deploy the program to customers"],"correct":2,"explain":"Testing exercises the program with a wide range of data — typical values, boundary values and invalid values — to expose logic errors before users meet them.","topic":"SDLC phases","id":"wr_p5_11","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which SDLC model moves through the phases in a strict, non-overlapping order?","options":["Agile","Prototyping","Spiral","Waterfall"],"correct":3,"explain":"Waterfall completes each phase before the next begins, which makes it simple to manage but hard to change once you are downstream. Agile deliberately iterates in short cycles instead.","topic":"SDLC models","id":"wr_p5_12","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which SDLC model delivers working software in short repeated cycles and welcomes changing requirements?","options":["Agile","The program development cycle","Big-bang integration","Waterfall"],"correct":0,"explain":"Agile works in short iterations, each producing something usable, so feedback can change the direction of the next cycle. That flexibility is exactly what Waterfall gives up.","topic":"SDLC models","id":"wr_p5_13","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A team builds a quick, incomplete version of the interface so users can react to it before the real system is built. Which approach is this?","options":["Regression testing","Prototyping","Waterfall","Maintenance"],"correct":1,"explain":"A prototype is a throwaway or partial build made to gather feedback early, when changes are still cheap.","topic":"SDLC models","id":"wr_p5_14","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which SDLC model is organised around repeated cycles that each include a risk analysis?","options":["Waterfall","Spiral","Prototyping","Agile"],"correct":1,"explain":"The spiral model repeats a loop of planning, risk analysis, engineering and evaluation — its distinguishing feature is that explicit risk assessment on every pass.","topic":"SDLC models","id":"wr_p5_15","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Why is documentation produced throughout the lifecycle rather than only at the end?","options":["It replaces the need for testing","Later maintainers need to understand the decisions, and the details are forgotten quickly","It makes the program run faster","It is required before a program can be compiled"],"correct":1,"explain":"Most of a program's life is maintenance, often by someone who did not write it. Documentation written as decisions are made is accurate; documentation written months later is guesswork.","topic":"SDLC phases","id":"wr_p5_16","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What is the purpose of a requirements document?","options":["To list the hardware in the computer lab","To record what the software must do, so the finished product can be checked against it","To describe how the compiler works","To record every bug found during testing"],"correct":1,"explain":"Requirements state what the system must do. They are the yardstick that acceptance testing measures the finished product against.","topic":"SDLC phases","id":"wr_p5_17","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which step comes immediately BEFORE coding the program?","options":["Test the program","Plan the logic","Put the program into production","Translate the code"],"correct":1,"explain":"The order is understand the problem, plan the logic, code the program, translate, test, put into production, maintain. Planning the logic is the last step before code is written.","topic":"Development cycle order","id":"wr_p5_18","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A user reports that a working payroll program must now handle a new tax rule. Which phase does this work belong to?","options":["Translation","Analysis","Testing","Maintenance"],"correct":3,"explain":"Changing a program that is already in production — for fixes, updates or new rules — is maintenance, the longest phase of the lifecycle.","topic":"SDLC phases","id":"wr_p5_19","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Why does the cycle put \"understand the problem\" before \"plan the logic\"?","options":["A plan can only be correct if it solves the right problem","Compilers require requirements as input","Planning tools are unavailable until requirements are approved","It shortens the testing phase"],"correct":0,"explain":"Solving the wrong problem elegantly is still failure, and the mistake is most expensive when it is discovered late. Understanding first is what makes the plan worth making.","topic":"Development cycle order","id":"wr_p5_20","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What does deployment (putting the program into production) mean?","options":["Making the finished program available to its intended users","Compiling the program for the first time","Writing the user documentation","Running the final round of tests"],"correct":0,"explain":"Deployment is the handover into real use. Testing happens before it, and maintenance follows it.","topic":"SDLC phases","id":"wr_p5_21","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which pair correctly maps development-cycle wording to lifecycle phases?","options":["\"Plan the logic\" = analysis, \"Code the program\" = design","\"Plan the logic\" = design, \"Code the program\" = implementation","\"Plan the logic\" = implementation, \"Code the program\" = design","\"Plan the logic\" = testing, \"Code the program\" = maintenance"],"correct":1,"explain":"The same work carries two vocabularies: planning the logic IS the design phase, and coding the program IS implementation. Questions often swap vocabularies mid-sentence to see whether you can map them.","topic":"SDLC phases","id":"wr_p5_22","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What is the main risk of skipping the planning step and coding immediately?","options":["The program will use too much memory","The compiler will refuse to translate the program","Logic errors and rework, because the structure was never thought through","The program cannot be documented afterwards"],"correct":2,"explain":"Code written without a plan tends to need restructuring once the gaps appear — the most expensive kind of rework. It is not a translation problem; the program may compile perfectly and still be wrong.","topic":"Development cycle","id":"wr_p5_23","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"During which step would you desk-check an algorithm by walking through it with sample values on paper?","options":["Plan the logic","Maintain the program","Put the program into production","Translate the code"],"correct":0,"explain":"Desk-checking tests the LOGIC before any code exists, which is the cheapest possible moment to find a flaw. It belongs with planning.","topic":"Development cycle","id":"wr_p5_24","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What does it mean that the SDLC is a cycle rather than a straight line?","options":["Each phase is performed by the same person","The phases may be completed in any order","Testing is repeated until the code compiles","Maintenance feeds new requirements back into analysis, starting the process again"],"correct":3,"explain":"Changes discovered during maintenance become new requirements, which re-enter analysis and design. That feedback is what makes it a cycle.","topic":"SDLC phases","id":"wr_p5_25","difficulty":"medium"}],"D684/write_drill/p6":[{"text":"Four workplace situations are described below. Which one violates both the ACM and the IEEE Codes of Ethics?","options":["A manager pays for a team member to attend a technical conference","A company makes employees sign the Code of Ethics annually as a condition of continued employment","An executive eliminates all professional development opportunities for employees","A factory immediately stops production when an environmental impact is discovered"],"correct":2,"explain":"Both codes require supporting colleagues' professional growth — ACM asks leaders to create opportunities for members to grow as professionals, and IEEE asks members to assist colleagues in their professional development. Removing all of it violates both. The other three are compliant: reaffirming the code, halting harm once discovered, and funding training are exactly what the codes ask for.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_1","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A developer copies a colleague's module into a product and presents the design as entirely their own. Which principle is violated?","options":["Protecting user privacy","Maintaining technical competence","Avoiding conflicts of interest","Giving proper credit for intellectual property and the work of others"],"correct":3,"explain":"Both codes require crediting the contributions of others and respecting the work required to produce new ideas. Passing off someone else's work as yours is a credit and honesty violation.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_2","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"An engineer accepts an expensive gift from a supplier while deciding which supplier wins a contract. Which principle is violated?","options":["Maintaining accurate documentation","Rejecting bribery and avoiding conflicts of interest","Improving public understanding of technology","Supporting colleagues' development"],"correct":1,"explain":"The IEEE code explicitly rejects bribery in all its forms and requires disclosing conflicts of interest; ACM requires honesty and avoiding situations that compromise professional judgement. Accepting a gift from a bidder you are judging is the textbook case.","topic":"IEEE","id":"wr_p6_3","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A team discovers a defect that could injure users but ships anyway to meet a deadline. Which principle is violated?","options":["Providing honest cost estimates","Crediting contributors","Holding paramount the safety, health, and welfare of the public","Attending professional development"],"correct":2,"explain":"Public safety is the first obligation in both codes — IEEE puts it first, and ACM requires avoiding harm. A deadline never outranks a known risk to people.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_4","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A programmer browses customer records out of curiosity, without any work reason to view them. Which principle is violated?","options":["Maintaining technical competence","Improving public understanding of computing","Accepting honest criticism","Respecting privacy and honoring confidentiality"],"correct":3,"explain":"Both codes require respecting privacy and accessing systems and data only when authorised. Having the technical ability to open a record is not the same as being permitted to.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_5","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A contractor states a system is \"fully tested and secure\" knowing that testing was never completed. Which principle is violated?","options":["Creating growth opportunities for staff","Avoiding discrimination","Supporting colleagues' professional development","Being honest and realistic in stating claims based on available data"],"correct":3,"explain":"Both codes demand honesty and trustworthiness; IEEE specifically requires claims and estimates to be honest and realistic and grounded in the available data. Overstating what was verified misleads whoever relies on it.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_6","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"An engineer accepts a project requiring expertise they do not have, without telling anyone about the gap. Which principle is violated?","options":["Giving credit to colleagues","Respecting user privacy","Undertaking technical tasks only when qualified, or after full disclosure of limitations","Rejecting bribery"],"correct":2,"explain":"Both codes limit work to areas of competence. Taking such a task is permitted only after the limitations are fully disclosed so others can judge the risk — quietly hoping to learn on the job is the violation.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_7","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A hiring manager rejects qualified applicants because of their age. Which principle is violated?","options":["Treating all persons fairly and not discriminating","Documenting design decisions","Maintaining technical competence","Avoiding conflicts of interest"],"correct":0,"explain":"Both codes require fair treatment and prohibit discrimination and harassment on grounds such as age, race, gender, disability or national origin.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_8","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A developer is shown a flaw in their algorithm by a peer reviewer and refuses to acknowledge or correct it. Which principle is violated?","options":["Rejecting bribery","Seeking, accepting, and offering honest criticism, and acknowledging and correcting errors","Creating professional development opportunities","Protecting the privacy of users"],"correct":1,"explain":"Both codes treat professional review as an obligation — IEEE requires acknowledging and correcting errors, and ACM requires accepting and providing appropriate professional review. Defensiveness that leaves a known defect in place is the violation.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_9","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"An employee spreads a false rumour that damages a co-worker's professional reputation. Which principle is violated?","options":["Maintaining technical competence","Respecting intellectual property","Avoiding injuring others, their property, reputation, or employment by false or malicious action","Honest cost estimation"],"correct":2,"explain":"The IEEE code names reputation and employment explicitly, and ACM requires being honest and trustworthy and avoiding harm to others.","topic":"IEEE","id":"wr_p6_10","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which of these is COMPLIANT with the ACM and IEEE codes rather than a violation?","options":["A developer copies licensed code into a product without permission","A developer hides a known security flaw to protect the company's reputation","A developer discloses a conflict of interest to their manager before joining a review panel","A developer accesses a friend's account records without authorisation"],"correct":2,"explain":"Disclosing a conflict is exactly what both codes require. The other three are violations of, in order, avoiding harm and honesty, intellectual property, and privacy and authorised access.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_11","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A company collects far more personal data than its service needs, \"in case it is useful later.\" Which principle does this most directly conflict with?","options":["Rejecting bribery","Respecting privacy, including collecting only the data actually needed","Giving credit for others' work","Maintaining technical competence"],"correct":1,"explain":"ACM requires respecting privacy, which includes collecting only what is necessary and being transparent about its use. Collecting speculatively increases harm if the data leaks.","topic":"ACM","id":"wr_p6_12","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A developer is asked to write code that will secretly mislead regulators. What does the code of ethics require?","options":["Comply, but document the objection privately","Ask a colleague to write it instead","Refuse — the codes require honesty and obeying the law, whatever the employer asks","Comply, because the employer accepts responsibility"],"correct":2,"explain":"Both codes require honesty and lawful conduct, and responsibility does not transfer to whoever gave the order. Delegating the same act to a colleague is no better.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_13","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"An engineer publishes a paper describing the limitations and risks of a technology as well as its benefits. How do the codes view this?","options":["A conflict of interest","A violation of intellectual property","Compliant — it improves public understanding of technology and its consequences","A violation of confidentiality"],"correct":2,"explain":"Both codes ask members to foster public awareness and understanding of computing and technology, including its potential consequences. Presenting limitations honestly is a duty, not a breach.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_14","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which best describes the purpose of a professional code of ethics?","options":["To protect employers from lawsuits","To state the profession's shared obligations and guide judgement in difficult situations","To define programming standards for each language","To replace national law"],"correct":1,"explain":"A code sets the profession's expectations and helps a member reason about hard cases. It supplements the law rather than replacing it, and it is about conduct, not syntax.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_15","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A system a team maintains has become part of critical public infrastructure. What extra obligation do the codes recognise?","options":["Only a documentation obligation","Reduced obligation, because the government now owns the risk","Extra care, because failures now carry consequences for the whole public","No change — the obligations are identical for every system"],"correct":2,"explain":"ACM asks members to recognise and take special care of systems that become integrated into the infrastructure of society, precisely because the cost of failure rises with dependence.","topic":"ACM","id":"wr_p6_16","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"During a security review, an engineer finds a flaw in a competitor's public product. What do the codes support?","options":["Ignoring it because it is a competitor","Reporting it responsibly to the vendor so it can be fixed","Using it to win customers","Publishing exploit code immediately"],"correct":1,"explain":"Avoiding harm to the public outranks competitive advantage. Responsible disclosure lets the flaw be fixed before it is exploited.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_17","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A manager pressures a tester to sign off on untested features. What should the tester do under the codes?","options":["Refuse to certify work that has not been verified, and state the risk","Sign, since the manager is accountable","Sign but note it in a private file","Resign without explanation"],"correct":0,"explain":"Both codes require honest claims and high-quality work. Certifying unverified work is a false statement, and the responsibility stays with the person who signs.","topic":"ACM & IEEE","id":"wr_p6_18","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"Which situation is a violation of the obligation to maintain technical competence?","options":["An engineer takes a course in a new framework","An engineer reads the release notes before upgrading","An engineer stops learning and continues using a method known to be unsafe","An engineer asks a colleague for a design review"],"correct":2,"explain":"IEEE requires maintaining and improving technical competence; ACM requires high standards of professional competence. Continuing with a method known to be unsafe fails both. The other three are how competence is maintained.","topic":"IEEE","id":"wr_p6_19","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"An employee uses company computing resources to run a private business without permission. Which principle is violated?","options":["Crediting the work of others","Providing honest estimates","Improving public understanding of technology","Accessing computing and communication resources only when authorised"],"correct":3,"explain":"ACM requires access to computing resources only when authorised or compelled by the public good. Unauthorised use is a violation even when nothing appears to break.","topic":"ACM","id":"wr_p6_20","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"A team ignores accessibility requirements, leaving disabled users unable to use a public service. How do the codes view this?","options":["A design preference, not an ethical matter","Acceptable if few users are affected","Acceptable if accessibility was not in the contract","A violation — the codes require fair treatment and systems that serve all users"],"correct":3,"explain":"ACM requires being fair and taking action not to discriminate, and asks that systems be usable by people with differing needs; contributing to society means not excluding part of it.","topic":"ACM","id":"wr_p6_21","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"What does the ACM code mean by \"avoid harm\"?","options":["Avoid negative consequences such as loss of information, property, or safety, especially when unjustified","Avoid criticising other professionals","Never release software with any defect","Avoid working on military systems"],"correct":0,"explain":"Avoiding harm means not causing unjustified negative consequences and minimising unintended ones — including data loss, property damage and injury. It is not a demand for perfection, nor a ban on criticism.","topic":"ACM","id":"wr_p6_22","difficulty":"medium"},{"text":"An engineer signs off on a design in a field they do not understand because a colleague assured them it was fine.
